solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shady soldiers let in subject to debate

indicators.note: the soldiers are admitted into the middle of the other word, so it holds them

parts.note: something open to argument is disputable
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A dodgy matter, with troops admitted to it, remains open to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady character has a poor reputation, which is what disreputable describes.

clue.text: Earnings right for a new arrival

parts.note: earnings are income

explanation.surface: Is a salary fair pay for someone just joining?
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has recently moved into a place or community.

clue.text: Restoration of control over what the bank may provide

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
a bank sends its customers a statement of their account

explanation.surface: Getting back control of what your bank gives you.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstatement is the act of putting something or someone back in a former position.

clue.text: Central European elegance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from Poland, in central Europe

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses differ in sound too: one has a long O, the other a short one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the adjective for the people of Poland and a noun for refined style.

clue.text: Moody doctor met male parent

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A sulky physician met his own father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun, a physician, but is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental person is liable to sudden changes of mood.

clue.text: Stick — at the crease, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short rod, as used by a conductor or relay runner
second meaning: a batsman at the crease in cricket is still batting on

explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line where the batsman stands in cricket; split the answer as BAT ON, carrying on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a thin stick, and split in two it describes a cricketer still in.

clue.text: Interminable — or without a goal?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lacking an end or aim

explanation.walkthrough: An end is an aim or goal, so something with no aim is end-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means having no finish, and literally it is an absence of any end or objective.

clue.text: Examination Charlie received in hospital

indicators.note: received in means taken into, so the letter goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is admitted to hospital for a check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is a medical examination of the body by imaging, or any close inspection.

clue.text: Spiny plants originally cleared before start of play

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word cleared

parts.note: a play starts with Act I, its first act

explanation.surface: A gardener clears away prickly growth before a game can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti is the plural of cactus, a desert succulent covered in spines.

clue.text: Told untruths about US university being inadequate

indicators.note: about means around, so the lying word goes round the university

parts.note: to tell untruths is to have lied
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone lied about an American college, which turns out to be second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limited is restricted in scope or ability, falling short of what is needed.

clue.text: Eastern chaps going west, initially sealing one's fate

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so backwards

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
chaps are men

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of sealing

parts.note: one's is read as one is, I'S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Men from the East head west, and this seals their destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, and the word now means one's inescapable downfall or doom.

clue.text: Fellow that is connected with English navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A man who has links to the English navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: E and RN first, then IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's first name, and crosswords freely use any male name for a fellow.

clue.text: Prohibition restricting member, one working in pub

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the prohibition word surrounds the limb

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: A ban that limits one member of staff who works in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves drinks behind the bar, so he is employed in a pub.

clue.text: Indian chap taking girl on island

parts.note: Ben is a man's name, a chap
gal is an informal word for girl
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An Indian man takes a young woman over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a native of Bengal, a region of India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Father and son crossing first of many treeless plains

indicators.note: crossing here means straddling, so father and son sit either side of the letter

parts.note: papa is a word for father

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of many

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father and son cross many open grasslands.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy lowlands of South America, with few or no trees.

clue.text: Demonstration in favour of international match

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A rally held in support of an international fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a public demonstration objecting to something.

clue.text: It may spoil radio reception — still!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crackling interference on the radio

explanation.walkthrough: The dash and exclamation mark make 'still' look like an adverb continuing the sentence; it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is both electrical noise heard on a radio and an adjective for something stationary.

clue.text: Initially nice old boy, the French aristocrat

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of nice

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A pleasant old chap turns out to be a French nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the aristocracy, a person of high hereditary rank.

clue.text: A solid block set up in wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slab is a solid block of stone or similar

explanation.surface: A solid chunk of material is erected in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical timber, used for models.

clue.text: Work hard enclosing judge's leafy plant

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the hard-work word wraps round the judge

parts.note: to toil is to work hard
a ref, or referee, is a judge in sport; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone toils away at a plant belonging to a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is clover or a similar plant whose leaves have three leaflets.

clue.text: Youth holding end of poodle's leash

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the youth wraps round the letter

parts.note: a lad is a youth

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word poodle

explanation.surface: A young man holds the poodle's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'poodle' is its E; the 's belongs to the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is the strap or cord attached to a dog's collar, the same thing as a leash.

clue.text: Complaint of large blokes in small island

indicators.note: in places the large blokes inside the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Large men on a tiny island have something to grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder, an ailment.

clue.text: In Egypt he taunted a character from Greece

indicators.note: In tells us the answer is sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: In Egypt a man teases a visitor from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Poor Italian curate leaves area, lacking fluency

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging
leaves means departs, so one letter is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A bad Italian priest walks out, unable to speak smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: ITALIAN CURATE has thirteen letters; drop one A for area, as 'leaves' says, and rearrange the rest as 'Poor' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An inarticulate person struggles to express themselves clearly in speech.
